prompt: Six weeks after hearing his updates were too long, an engineer tells his manager, 'I've been capping them at five bullets. Is that working for you?'
tells: 'I've been capping them at five bullets. Is that working for you?'
why: Show what you changed and check it helped.
trap: Shorter updates are the change; the move is reporting back.

prompt: A peer once said a lead's design reviews felt rushed. A month later, the lead messages her: 'I've moved them to 45 minutes after your note. Thanks again.'
tells: 'I've moved them to 45 minutes after your note.
why: Telling people their feedback mattered makes them give more.
trap: There's thanks, but the move is the follow-up.

prompt: After an engagement survey, a director shares at the all-hands the three things employees raised and what has changed for each.
tells: the three things employees raised and what has changed for each
trap: She isn't asking for more detail; she's showing action.

prompt: A manager who gave feedback about missed deadlines books a check-in a month later to review how it's gone since.
tells: books a check-in a month later to review how it's gone since
why: Follow up on feedback over time.
trap: The request was made earlier; this is checking back.

prompt: In an interview, a candidate describes going back to the reviewer who criticized their testing to show the new checklist they'd built.
tells: going back to the reviewer who criticized their testing
why: Return to the source and show the change.
trap: It's after acting on it, not in the moment.

prompt: A support lead emails a customer who reported a confusing setting: 'We shipped a new label based on your report this week.'
tells: 'We shipped a new label based on your report this week.'
why: Tell people what their feedback changed.
trap: It isn't praise; it's reporting an outcome.
